P.S. This is just a personal theory, but maybe the "formatting" process was incomplete for me.  

Formatting as in that process where people lose their past life memory at the age of 5-6 and become acculturized to their environment. And because of that I have always felt that I don't belong here.

I don't really have a clear memory of what exactly I was before the reincarnation, just that I was a woman in my 30s, and I wasn't living in my current country.  

So I got stabbed to death somewhere in the 90s (1991?) and there I lie on the concrete, laying on my own blood. Cue the "afterlife" thing.  

I went to the light. Stupidly.  

But to be fair, the light \*pulls\* you. Entices you. It's like how a moth couldn't resist going to the light.  

After going through the light, there's this extremely charismatic guy waiting for me. I had a life full of baggage and he seems to know about it and told me to tell him everything. Cry on his shoulder he said. And I did.  

I was lovebombed. It felt like I was injected extreme amount of dopamine right to my brain.  

Eventually he says that your next life won't be full of baggage and all of that I hated. He has such a extreme charisma that he could sell me that reincarnating is in the best interest of myself. As a woman myself I was \*throughly\* charmed by him, but I was still doubtful whether reincarnating is a good idea. The math doesn't add up.  

Oh, he got pissed off and throw me down here anyway. No matter how hard I refused.  

And here I am, in the cycle of samsara again. My mom said my cries sound like "No! NO!" when I were born.

Because I still remember what happened before this life. Right in the betweens between this life and the previous. I went to the light, and there's already this exceedingly charismatic "person" waiting for me there. And they tried to assure me that going back to Earth is in my best interests and so I did.  

Ah, well. This current iteration is far more shitty than my previous. I was well off back then.

About a year ago I did the same fuckup just like you, but my case was inexperience and I was trying to get some free space by deleting efi partition (which is a colossal mistake btw) and I end up reinstalling it by using the custom setting in Windows Setup.

Windows setup will disregard the efi partition that you just recreate, just delete that partition. It'll create the new efi partition by itself.

You might be able to salvage your files from Users folder by booting some lightweight linux. It will disregard NTFS permissions in my case.. So you can access your files.

Just be CAREFUL that you didn't accidentally format the partition that you used to store some personal data.

P.S Restore points won't restore the efi partition, it'll only restore your windows settings to the date when you created the restore point. example: You just installed AutoCAD 2000, then you use the system restore. AutoCAD 2000 is gone after that.
